newsitem.title: CHILE: Latam stocks buoyant, but profit-taking expected.
newsitem.headline: Latam stocks buoyant, but profit-taking expected.

text.p: Investors can expect a smooth ride in most Latin American stock markets this week, but profit taking could undermine recent surges in several bourses, traders said.

Only the Caracas bolsa is expected to remain unsettled as soaring markets elsewhere in the region attract foreign investors with local players hanging back on a rash of public sector labor diputes, they said.
Venezuela's 19-share IBCC index closed last week down 0.8 percent at 6,469.84 points in slow trade.
"First the doctors went on strike, then the teachers and now it's investors," said Credit Lyonnais broker Peter Ryan in New York.
The mood, however, in other markets in Latin America is expected to continue bullish with stocks resuming their upward march this week bolstered with buy orders from New York.
Chilean stocks continued their New Year rally Monday, climbing by more than one percent by midsession with heavyweight electricity stocks among the leading gainers, traders said.
But dealers were divided as to whether the market would hit the profit-taking buffer seen looming this week over the Sao Paulo and Mexican bourses.
"I doubt people will take profits as they have bought stocks so cheaply," said Pablo Salcedo, head of research at ING Barings.
Other traders said they thought players could move to cash in gains from the stronger-than-expected 14 percent rise in stocks since the start of the year.
The selective IPSA index climbed five percent last week to 113.2 points.
In Brazil, stocks are seen posting further gains but the bolsa could lose strength on profit-taking after the bolsa's recent surge, said traders.

Foreign capital inflows, which have been the driving force behind the rally, could slow this week because of the impact of a new financial tax on foreign investment which officially comes into force Thursday, said traders.
The selective Bovespa index ended last week up 4.5 percent at 78,163 points.
After climbing nearly five percent last week, Mexican shares are seen pausing for breath this week with a slowdown expected in trading by foreign investors, said traders.
"We now see some prices levelling off, and although the bolsa is strong, it needs to rest," said an analyst at brokerage CBI.
Technical analysis which have shown the market may be overbought could mean that the leading IPC share index, which rose 4.81 percent last week, could fall to 3,650 points.

Argentine stocks were expected to overcome a mild bout of profit-taking and resume their upward march, with investors betting on a successful launch of Argentina's global bond between Tuesday and Wednesday.
"The global bond deal is underpinning the market, which still has strong upside potential," said analyst Maximiliano Goff at Rio Research.
"The present correction is just part of the normal process of consolidation."
The bolsa's blue-chip MerVal index pulled back 1.5 percent at the end of last week, paring the week's gains to 0.9 percent.
((-- Santiago newsroom, 562-699-5595x212))
